name: Niger Military Coup
description: Presidential guard led by Gen. Tchiani detained President Bazoum and seized power, forming the CNSP. Bazoum remains detained at the presidential palace.

name: ECOWAS Standby Force Activation Against Niger
description: ECOWAS ordered activation of standby force after Niger junta ignored ultimatum. Mali and Burkina Faso warned intervention would be a 'declaration of war.'

name: JNIM Blockade of Timbuktu
description: JNIM imposed a complete blockade on Timbuktu, cutting off food supplies, humanitarian aid, and commercial flights. Food prices doubled.

name: Gabon Military Coup
description: Military officers seized power minutes after Ali Bongo was declared election winner, ending the Bongo family's 56-year rule.

name: Alliance of Sahel States (AES) Formation
description: Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger signed the Charter of Liptako-Gourma establishing a mutual defense alliance. Article VI: attack on one is attack on all.

name: Malian Army / Wagner Capture of Kidal
target: City of Kidal, Tuareg rebel stronghold
description: Malian army backed by Wagner mercenaries captured Kidal, ending over a decade of Tuareg rebel control. Wagner flew their flag over the fort on November 22.

name: Zaongo Village Massacre by Burkinabe Army
description: The Burkinabe army massacred at least 70 people in Zaongo village in Yatenga Province. Reports range from 70 to over 200 killed.

name: Plateau State Christmas Eve Massacres
target: 17+ rural communities in Bokkos and Barkin Ladi
description: Armed attackers systematically attacked villages across Plateau State on Christmas Eve in one of Nigeria's worst sectarian attacks.

name: Last French Troops Leave Niger
description: The last 1,500 French soldiers departed Niger, ending a decade of French counterterrorism operations in the Sahel. France also closed its embassy.

name: MINUSMA Completes Withdrawal from Mali
description: The UN completed its full withdrawal from Mali per Security Council Resolution 2690, ending 10 years of peacekeeping operations.

name: Russia's Africa Corps Deploys to Burkina Faso
description: Russia's Africa Corps deployed 100 military personnel with plans to expand to 300. Base established at Loumbila, 20 km northeast of Ouagadougou.

name: AES States Announce ECOWAS Withdrawal
description: The three AES juntas jointly announced ECOWAS withdrawal, citing sanctions and intervention threats. Withdrawal became effective January 29, 2025.

name: Nondin and Soro Village Massacres
target: Nondin and Soro villages, Yatenga Province
description: Burkinabe soldiers summarily executed at least 223 civilians, including 56 children. Human Rights Watch described it as the worst army abuse since 2015, possibly crimes against humanity.

name: Kuriga School Mass Kidnapping
target: Students at Kuriga schools, Kaduna State
description: Armed men abducted 287 students aged 8-15 from schools in Kuriga, demanding 1 billion naira ransom. All freed after 17 days.

name: Russia's Africa Corps Arrives in Niger
description: One hundred Africa Corps troops arrived in Niamey with a 'latest generation' air defense system to train Nigerien forces.

name: Niger Revokes Orano Uranium Mining License
description: Niger revoked Orano's license at the Imouraren mine (200,000 tonnes uranium). Orano halted all production at Arlit by October 31.

name: AES Confederation Treaty Signed
description: AES leaders signed a confederation treaty transforming the mutual defense pact into a full confederation with economic integration goals, free from Western influence.

name: US Forces Withdraw from Niamey Air Base 101
description: US forces completed withdrawal from Air Base 101 in Niamey following Niger's termination of the bilateral defense agreement.

name: Battle of Tinzaouaten
description: Tuareg rebels ambushed a Malian-Wagner convoy in a three-day battle. Wagner's largest known loss of life in Africa, with possibly only three Russian fighters surviving.

name: US Completes Withdrawal from Agadez Air Base 201
description: US completed withdrawal from Air Base 201 near Agadez, a $110 million drone base and the largest USAF-led construction project in history.

name: Barsalogho Massacre
description: JNIM attacked hundreds of civilians forced by the military to dig defensive trenches. The deadliest massacre in Burkinabe history and deadliest single attack of the Sahel insurgency.

name: Djibo Siege Humanitarian Emergency
description: MSF suspended operations in Djibo after recurrent attacks. Residents had less than 3L of water per day, resorted to eating leaves.

name: Attack on Chad Presidential Palace
description: 24 attackers armed with knives and machetes attempted to storm the presidential complex. President Deby was inside but unharmed.

name: AES States Formally Leave ECOWAS
description: Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso officially left ECOWAS after a one-year notice period.

name: AES Joint Operation Yereko 2
target: Jihadist groups in Liptako-Gourma tri-border area
description: The three AES armies conducted a tripartite joint operation targeting jihadist sanctuaries in the tri-border area.

name: JNIM Fuel Blockade of Southern Mali
target: Fuel supply routes from Senegal, Guinea, Ivory Coast
description: JNIM announced a fuel blockade destroying over 300 tankers on national roads, crippling 95% of Mali's fuel imports.

name: AES Launches Unified Military Force (FU-AES)
description: The AES inaugurated a 5,000-strong unified military force with headquarters in Niamey, integrating air power, intelligence sharing, and coordinated ground operations.

name: ISSP/ISWAP Assault on Niamey Airport & Air Base 101
target: Diori Hamani International Airport and Air Base 101, Niamey
casualties: Niger: 20 attackers killed, 11 captured, 4 soldiers wounded (official); unconfirmed reports of 24 Nigerien soldiers and 3–4 Russian personnel killed
description: 30+ Islamic State militants on motorcycles, using drones and mortars, attacked Niamey's airport and the adjoining Air Base 101 in the early hours, destroying at least five military aircraft including a helicopter and damaging Air Côte d'Ivoire and Asky airliners. Gen. Tiani accused France, Benin and Côte d'Ivoire of sponsoring the attack without presenting evidence; the US moved Niger to Level 4 'Do Not Travel' the next day.
sources: Wikipedia (Al Jazeera / France 24 / AP / Long War Journal citations) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_2026_Diori_Hamani_International_Airport_attack

name: JNIM/FLA Coordinated Attack on Kati Military Base
target: Kati military base, Defense Minister Sadio Camara
casualties: Defense Minister Camara killed; Intelligence Chief Kone killed April 26; Army Chief Diarra wounded
description: JNIM drove a car bomb into the Defense Minister's house. President Goita evacuated. Part of the largest coordinated offensive since the 2012 northern Mali capture.

name: JNIM Attack on Sevare Airfield
target: Sevare military airfield and Mopti area
casualties: Unknown; city split between government and rebel control
description: JNIM attacked the strategic Sevare airfield hosting Mali Air Force and Russian forces. The city was split under dual control.

name: Tuareg/JNIM Alliance Recaptures Kidal
description: In unprecedented alliance, Tuareg separatists and JNIM jointly recaptured Kidal, reversing the November 2023 victory. Africa Corps confirmed withdrawal on April 27. Update: the Malian army, with Africa Corps, re-entered Kidal on 6 Oct 2026 after the FLA announced a 'strategic withdrawal'; the town is back under government control.

name: ISSP Seizes Labbezanga Border Post
target: Labbezanga border post on Mali-Niger frontier
description: ISSP forces captured Labbezanga, a key post on the Mali-Niger border, after Malian and Russian forces withdrew during the broader April 25 offensive. ISSP subsequently began probing military positions around the regional capital Menaka.

name: JNIM Reimpose Full Blockade on Bamako
target: Bamako supply routes and 4 million residents
description: Two days after the April 25 offensive, JNIM announced a full blockade of Bamako, establishing checkpoints on all approaches and halting incoming and outgoing traffic. By April 30 over 250 vehicles were stranded on blocked roads.

name: FLA and JNIM Capture Tessalit Military Base
target: Tessalit military base near Algerian border
description: FLA and JNIM seized the Tessalit military base after Malian and Russian forces withdrew southward. The capture completed rebel consolidation of the entire Kidal Region including Aguelhok and Anefis. Update: Malian army convoys reoccupied Anefis and Aguelhok on 3–5 Oct 2026; Tessalit's status was unconfirmed as of 13 Oct.

name: Goita Assumes Defense Ministry After Camara Death
description: President Assimi Goita appointed himself Defense Minister following Sadio Camara's death in the April 25 attacks. The move consolidated all political and military authority under Goita as the junta faced its gravest crisis.

name: JNIM Storms Kenieroba Central Prison
description: JNIM fighters stormed Kenieroba Central Prison, dubbed Africa's Alcatraz, located 60 km southwest of Bamako. The facility held 2,500 prisoners including 72 high-value detainees and captured JNIM fighters. Attackers set vehicles ablaze inside the compound.

name: JNIM Village Attacks Kill 70+ in Mopti Region
target: Villages of Korikori, Gomossogou, Kouroude, and Dougara
description: JNIM attacked multiple villages in Mopti Region over two days. On May 7 fighters killed over 30 in Korikori and Gomossogou in apparent retaliation against Dan Na Ambassagou militia. On May 8, 40 more were killed in Kouroude and Dougara.

name: JNIM Landmine Kills 8 on Bamako-Kayes Highway
description: A JNIM landmine detonated under a civilian bus on the Bamako-Kayes highway, killing eight and injuring 42. The attack illustrated JNIM's ability to disrupt transport corridors across southern Mali during the ongoing blockade.

name: Second Coordinated FLA/JNIM Offensive Across Mali
target: Anefis, Gao, Aguelhok, Bandiagara, Kati, Kenieroba prison
casualties: 30+ soldiers killed; Mali claimed 100 militants killed
description: FLA and JNIM launched a second coordinated offensive after a two-month operational pause, simultaneously attacking Anefis, Gao, Aguelhok, Bandiagara, Kati, and again the Kenieroba prison. Anefis was the primary target with FLA claiming control of the town.

name: FLA Shoots Down Russian Mi-24 Near Anefis
target: Africa Corps Mi-24P helicopter and relief convoy
casualties: Helicopter crew killed; additional convoy casualties unknown
description: FLA fighters ambushed an Africa Corps relief convoy moving from Gao toward Anefis and shot down a Mi-24P attack helicopter near Tabrichat. The shootdown was verified by OSINT analysts and marked a significant escalation in rebel anti-aircraft capability.

name: Jihadist Ambush Kills 16 Niger Soldiers in Tillaberi
target: Niger military liaison detachment on Bankilare-Tera axis
casualties: 16 soldiers killed, 23 wounded; 15 attackers reportedly killed
description: Jihadist fighters ambushed a Niger military liaison mission near Doungouro village on the Bankilare-Tera axis in Tillaberi Region. Reinforcements from Tera and air support forced the attackers to retreat. The AU Commission condemned the attack.

name: FLA Ambushes Mali Convoy Near Anefis
target: Malian-Africa Corps relief convoy returning from Anefis
description: FLA fighters ambushed a Malian-Africa Corps convoy on the return route from Anefis, where government forces had briefly recaptured the town on July 9. The FLA claimed 50 soldiers killed and 20 captured.

name: JNIM Overruns Kouakourou, Shoots Down Helicopter
target: Kouakourou military camp and town in Mopti Region
casualties: Multiple soldiers killed; Mi-24 helicopter crew killed
description: JNIM overran the military camp in Kouakourou in the Cercle de Djenne, forcing the population to flee. When three helicopters were dispatched the next day to evacuate casualties, JNIM fighters shot down and destroyed one Mi-24, killing its crew.

name: JNIM Attacks San Barracks in Segou Region
target: San military barracks in Segou Region
casualties: 10 soldiers and 40 militants killed (Malian army figures)
description: JNIM claimed full control of the army barracks in San, Segou Region, releasing video of fighters inside the base. The Malian army disputed this, stating the attack was repelled and the facility remained under government control.

name: Mali PM Maiga in Algiers as Ties Thaw
description: Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maiga met President Tebboune in Algiers after the two states restored diplomatic ties in July 2026, ending more than a year of rupture. The visit produced an invitation for Goita to visit Algeria, and Algeria's PM went to Bamako in mid-September. AFP sources later said Algeria may have asked Tuareg rebels not to resist the army's October push on Kidal.

name: Army Mutiny Hits Niamey Airport Base and Palace Area
target: Air Base 101 at Diori Hamani airport, presidential palace area, state broadcaster RTN
casualties: Dozens of soldiers reported killed or arrested
description: Soldiers, reportedly from Ouallam, Tera and Dosso units that had suffered heavy losses to IS-Sahel, detained comrades and opened fire at sensitive sites after midnight. The state broadcaster went off air. The junta said it regained control within hours, and the AES called it a destabilisation plot. Two weeks later Tiani replaced the army chief of staff.

name: JNIM Overruns Dioura Camp, ~100 Soldiers Killed
target: Malian army camp at Dioura, central Mali
casualties: At least 100 soldiers and 5 Africa Corps personnel killed; dozens captured (AFP/RFI sources; unconfirmed by army)
description: JNIM stormed and claimed full control of the Dioura camp. First AFP tolls of at least 50 soldiers roughly doubled within days, and JNIM videos showed dozens of prisoners. The army said only that it neutralised dozens of attackers. It is the deadliest single attack on the army in this window. Approximate coordinates.

name: Tiani Replaces Niger Army Chief After Mutiny
target: Chief of staff of the armed forces
description: General Tiani replaced chief of staff Moussa Salaou Barmou with Mamane Sani Kiaou without giving a reason, two weeks after the Aug 29 mutiny in Niamey.

name: JNIM Burns Fuel Convoys on Senegal-Bamako Route
target: Army-escorted fuel convoys from Senegal (Diedieni-Kolokani, Sep 13; Kaniera-Lakamane, Sep 14)
casualties: About 20 trucks burned; some escort soldiers killed or captured (RFI local sources)
description: JNIM hit an escorted fuel convoy about 100 km from Bamako on Sep 13, and the next day a convoy of more than 80 tankers near Kaniera-Lakamane. This showed the fuel blockade on the capital still enforced in mid-September. The army said only that it had responded vigorously.

name: US DFC Approves $414M for Niger's Dasa Uranium Mine
description: The US DFC approved a debt facility of up to $414 million for Global Atomic's Dasa project, two years after US troops left Niger. A week later Niamey raised its stake in the Madaouela uranium project from 10% to 40%. The pair marks a re-opening of Niger's uranium sector to Western capital on junta terms. Approximate coordinates.

name: Militants Hit Kassela Checkpoint Near Bamako
target: Kassela checkpoint, about 36 km from Bamako
description: On the night of Sep 18–19, militants struck a checkpoint on the capital's eastern approach while a drone hit a hangar at the Sevare base in central Mali. Both came days before Mali's 66th independence anniversary, at which Goita acknowledged the violence. Approximate coordinates.

name: IS-Sahel Attack on Dabagu Base Kills 38 Soldiers
target: Dabagu military base, Tahoua region, near the Malian border
casualties: 38 soldiers killed, several missing (Niger Ministry of Defence)
description: IS-Sahel attacked the Dabagu base, about 450 km from Niamey, on Wednesday Sep 23. The Defence Ministry announced it the next day alongside a same-day attack at Abala. Together they are the deadliest day for Niger's forces in this window. Approximate coordinates (Tillia area); the base was not precisely located in reporting.

name: IS-Sahel Attack at Abala Kills 19 Gendarmes
target: Security post at Abala, Filingue department, Tillaberi region
casualties: 19 military police or gendarmes killed (Niger Ministry of Defence)
description: This was the second IS-Sahel attack of Sep 23, about 250 km from Niamey, bringing the day's toll to at least 57 security personnel. English wires say military police; Belga says gendarmes.

name: Malian Drone Strikes Ahead of Kidal Push
target: FLA and JNIM positions near Anefis, Kidal and Tinzaouaten
casualties: At least 10 militants killed (Malian officials); FLA alleges civilian casualties
description: On Oct 4–6, Malian forces struck FLA and JNIM positions near Anefis, Kidal town and Tinzaouaten, reportedly with Turkish TB2 and Akinci drones. This followed an Oct 3 convoy of nearly 300 vehicles from Gao to the Anefis bases, then convoys to Aguelhok and Kidal.

name: Malian Army Retakes Kidal as FLA Withdraws
description: Malian troops backed by Africa Corps entered Kidal five months after FLA and JNIM took it in April. The FLA called it a temporary, controlled withdrawal under Russian air attack. It said the army entered without a fight, while the government described intense air-ground operations. The army then announced an offensive in the In-Tassik, Tin-Assalak and Abeibara sectors.

name: Niger Reaches $203M IMF Staff-Level Deal
description: The IMF reached a staff-level agreement with Niger on a $203 million, 38-month Extended Credit Facility, pending Executive Board approval in December. It is the junta's main external financing lifeline in the window.
